traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria and requirements in docs/stories/007.0-DEV-ERROR-REPORTING.story.md are fully implemented and verified.
Concrete evidence from the rule implementations shows that: - Each relevant rule (`require-story-annotation`, `require-req-annotation`, `require-branch-annotation`, `valid-annotation-format`, `valid-story-reference`, `valid-req-reference`) defines specific, convention-aligned messages in meta.messages with appropriate placeholders ({{name}}/{{functionName}}, {{missing}}, {{details}}, {{path}}, {{reqId}}, {{storyPath}}). - Error reports wire these messages through ESLint’s context.report with rich data, providing precise location and context. - At least `require-story-annotation` exposes ESLint suggestions for how to fix missing annotations, and tests assert on suggestion descriptions and fix functions. - Severity mapping matches the story’s conventions: missing annotations/references are errors; format issues are warnings, as enforced by TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES and verified by config tests. - Edge cases such as filesystem errors, invalid config regexes, and rule loading failures are handled gracefully with clear diagnostics, satisfying the Error Handling criterion. - Dedicated tests (especially tests/rules/error-reporting.test.ts) explicitly reference this story and its requirement IDs and confirm the expected message templates, data fields, and suggestions. A full Jest run (`npm test -- --verbose`) passes, confirming all these behaviors are currently working.
Based on this concrete evidence, Story 007.0-DEV-ERROR-REPORTING is fully implemented and passing.
